To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bryostatin-1-induced apoptosis of human prostate cancer cells is dependent on the presence and activity of PKC alpha.

bryostatin induces apoptosis of LNCCaP cells by activating the mitogen- activated protein kinase pathway and that this pathway is activated through prolonged translocation of extracellular-regu-lated protein kinase 1 and extracellular-regulated protein kinase 2 to non-nuclear membrane compartments.

the bryostatin analog 10 nM 12-deoxyphorbol 13-phenylacetate (DPP) induces prolonged translocation and down regulation of protein kinase C alpha (PKCalpha) in and apoptosis of human LNCaP prostate cancer cells, and that overexpression of PKC alpha in LNCaPs blocks the ability of 10 n M DPP to induce apoptosis, but not to induce prolonged translocation of other PKC isozymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of action of bryostatin, a novel anticancer drug that induces prolonged activation of PKCalpha in and death of LNCaPC cells overexpressing PKCalpha.
the role of PKCalpha in TPA-induced apoptosis of LNCapa human prostate cancer cells and the role of bryostatin in blocking TPA-induced apoptosis in these cells.
the mechanism of action of bryostatin, which is being evaluated for the treatment of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bryostatin-1-induced prolonged activation of Raf-1, mitogen-activated-protein kinases 1/2, and apoptosis in PKCalpha-transfected LNCAP cells is a result of the inability of bryostatin to down-regulate PKCalpha.
the prolonged membrane-associated PKCalpha is a critical component of the PKC activator (bryostatin 10 nM) induced apoptosis in LNCa P cells.

bryostatin-induced prolonged membrane-associated PKCa and PKCdelta/epsilon and prolonged activation of extracellur-regulated protein kinases 2 and 1/2 are necessary and sufficient to induce apoptosis of human prostate cancer LNCaP cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PKCalpha isoform is a critical determinant for PKC activator-induced LNCaP cell apoptosis and that bryostatin-1 induced prolonged activation of extracelluar regulated protein kinase in PKCalpha transfectant cells, which is a critical step for bryostatin-induced apoptosis.

the PKC activators TPA and bryostatin induce prolonged activation of extracelular-regulated/mitogen activated protein kinases in LNCa P cells, that prolonged activation is dependent on the presence of PKCalpha on the membrane, and that prolonged activation of extraceullular regulated/mitogen-activated kinases is required for TPA-mediated apoptosis of LNCap cells.
PKC activators induce apoptosis in prostate cancer cells by inducing prolonged activation of PKCalpha.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bryostatin, an agent with a very low toxicity profile, can be used in combination with other agents that target other pathways to induce apoptosis in prostate cancer.
bryostatin-1-induced apoptosis of LNCap cells is mediated through the prolonged activation of extracellualr regulated kinase 1 and 1/2.
PKCalpha is not a necessary mediator of bryostatin's anti-cancer effects in LNCaPs.
